phenytoin.t: Folic acid therapy in folate-deficient individuals may decrease serum levels of phenytoin.

Enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants such as phenytoin, primidone, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and the broader anticonvulsant class increase hepatic folate metabolism, inhibit intestinal folate-processing enzymes, raise gastrointestinal pH, or displace folate from serum proteins, collectively leading to decreased folate availability.

methotrexate.t: Folic acid supplements are usually avoided on the day of oral methotrexate administration.
Several antifolate agents, including trimethoprim, pyrimethamine, methotrexate, and triamterene, directly inhibit dihydrofolate reductase, decreasing the formation of active folate derivatives.
